How to write in Hebrew (required in every Hebrew text you return):
- Spoken Israeli Hebrew, like a business owner talking to a regular customer. Not a translation from English: rephrase the idea, don't swap words.
- No literal translations. Not "how the business sounds" but "the business's style"; not "in your voice" but "the way you talk"; not "based on" or "driven by" but "according to"; not "make a difference," "at the end of the day," or "take it further" — say the thing itself; not "experience," "solution," or "journey" — call it by its name.
- Address in the plural (you all, yours, come). Not singular (you).
- Short sentences, one idea per sentence. No em dash (—) in headings. In the rest of the text, at most one em dash per paragraph; usually a comma, colon, or period is better.
- No agency or high-tech words: not "premium," "innovative," "customer experience," "content," "conversions," "leads," "engagement," and no English abbreviations.
- No generic openers and clichés: not "Hi everyone," "Looking for...?", "It's time to...," "We're happy to present," "We're waiting for you," "Don't miss out," "Treat yourselves." Open with a real detail from the business: a product, a time, a number, a moment.
- No English slang in Hebrew letters: not "ba-front," "the personal touch," "focus," "boost," "targeting" — write "at the forefront," "personal attention," "to focus," "to promote," "to address."
